layers.title: Source systems
layers.purpose: Know exactly what each source promises and how it changes, before reading a single row.

challenges.title: No contract with the source
challenges.goes_wrong: The source team renames or drops a column without telling anyone; loads break or quietly load the wrong thing.
challenges.example: Day 7, one plant's lab system renames defect_code to defect.
challenges.solution: One data contract per source dataset (columns, types, keys, personal-data class, freshness), checked at every load; a change outside the contract stops the batch and names the column.

challenges.title: Deletes are not signalled
challenges.goes_wrong: Rows vanish at the source and nothing downstream knows, so deleted orders keep counting.
challenges.example: Day 4, five order lines deleted in the order system; day 9, a nightly full copy arrives 40% short.
challenges.solution: Change feeds carry a delete marker; full copies are compared with what silver holds now, and a copy that would delete more than the declared share is held, not loaded.

adr.title: History kind follows dataset kind; deletes are soft

challenges.title: Full copies versus change feeds
challenges.goes_wrong: Reading a full copy every run is slow and hides deletes; reading a change feed without a starting copy misses history.
challenges.example: Materials arrive as a nightly full copy; order lines as a change feed.
challenges.solution: Each dataset declares how it is extracted (full copy, change feed, stream, paged interface) and how history is handed over to incremental loads.

challenges.title: Time zones and business dates
challenges.goes_wrong: Timestamps without a zone, or a day cut at midnight UTC, put production on the wrong business day.
challenges.example: Plants in India and Hungary record press readings in local time.
challenges.solution: Each source declares its time zone; the business date per plant is computed once in gold from a shared calendar.

challenges.title: Paged interfaces and rate limits
challenges.goes_wrong: A page fails halfway or the interface throttles, and the load either stops or skips records.
challenges.example: The dealer interface serves 200 records a page; a new dealer appears late (days 11 and 12).
challenges.solution: One batch per page with a cursor bookmark; retries only for passing failures; a reload of a paged interface is logged as a no-op because bronze is the replay point.

adr.title: Push lands files; pull goes straight to bronze through the lander steps

challenges.title: Files resent or late
challenges.goes_wrong: A partner sends the same file twice under a new name, or sends last month's file weeks late.
challenges.example: Day 5, dealer D-0042's October file arrives late; day 6, it is resent.
challenges.solution: The batch key is the file's content checksum, so a resend is refused; each file drop declares how many deliveries a period expects, so lateness is visible from the due day.

challenges.title: Personal data at the source
challenges.goes_wrong: Contact details flow into every layer in clear text.
challenges.example: Dealer contact email and phone, lab inspector ids.
challenges.solution: The contract marks each column's personal-data class; restricted columns are tokenised before they are first stored.

anti_patterns.title: Trusting the source to announce its changes
anti_patterns.why: Changes arrive unannounced; the first sign is a wrong number in a report.
anti_patterns.instead: Check every load against a written contract and stop on a change.

anti_patterns.title: Copying the whole source every run when a change feed exists
anti_patterns.why: Slow and costly, and deletes stay invisible unless every copy is compared.
anti_patterns.instead: Declare the extraction kind per dataset; use change feeds where offered and guard full copies.

layers.title: Ingestion
layers.purpose: Bring every delivery in exactly once, with a recorded outcome, through one set of entry steps.

challenges.title: Push and pull behave differently
challenges.goes_wrong: Files pushed by a source and data pulled by the platform go through different code, so the same problem is caught on one path and missed on the other.
challenges.example: Partner files are pushed; the order database is pulled.
challenges.solution: Pushed files land and go through the lander; pulled data runs the same lander steps in the same process, straight to bronze.

adr.title: Push lands files; pull goes straight to bronze through the lander steps

challenges.title: Reruns that double the data
challenges.goes_wrong: A retried load appends the same rows again.
challenges.example: A failed run is restarted halfway through a day.
challenges.solution: Every batch has a key; bronze writes replace by batch key, and a run restarts after the last batch the file log shows as loaded.

challenges.title: Duplicate deliveries
challenges.goes_wrong: The same content arrives twice and is counted twice.
challenges.example: Day 6, the partner file resent under a new name.
challenges.solution: The content checksum is the batch key; the landing area refuses a second write of the same delivery.

challenges.title: Partial or empty deliveries
challenges.goes_wrong: A half-written file or an empty batch is loaded as if complete.
challenges.example: A lab file arrives with three rows on a day that normally has hundreds.
challenges.solution: A declared volume band per dataset; empty and out-of-band batches are held with the reason in the file log; every file ends with a recorded outcome.

challenges.title: Large history loads and backfills
challenges.goes_wrong: Loading years of history through the daily path overwhelms it, or the handover to daily loads loses or repeats a day.
challenges.example: Backfilling a month of order lines.
challenges.solution: Reload and backfill are declared run types with a plan in the metadata store; the handover point is recorded.

challenges.title: Credentials in code
challenges.goes_wrong: Passwords in notebooks or repositories leak and cannot be rotated.
challenges.example: Database and interface credentials for four sources.
challenges.solution: Secrets resolved at run time from the secret store, per environment; never in the repository.

challenges.title: Schema drift at the door
challenges.goes_wrong: A changed column loads into the wrong place or as nulls.
challenges.example: Day 7, the renamed lab column.
challenges.solution: The contract check stops the batch and names the column; new columns are kept aside or stop the batch, as the dataset declares.

anti_patterns.title: Overwriting a file of the same name in landing
anti_patterns.why: If a resend overwrites a file, we cannot tell what was loaded, and a replay gives a different answer.
anti_patterns.instead: Give every delivery a unique name, list it in the manifest, and send corrections as new files.

anti_patterns.title: Reading landing files from anything but the lander
anti_patterns.why: A job that reads raw files skips tokenising, contract checks and the file log, so its output has no lineage.
anti_patterns.instead: Read bronze, which holds every record as received with full provenance.

anti_patterns.title: Hard-coded settings in notebooks
anti_patterns.why: Paths, thresholds and keys buried in code differ between copies, and nobody can see or audit them.
anti_patterns.instead: Put the value in YAML at the right level (platform, source, dataset or column) and read it from the metadata store.

anti_patterns.title: A copy-pasted pipeline per table
anti_patterns.why: A fix must be made fifty times, and the copies drift apart.
anti_patterns.instead: Add the table as metadata to the common pipeline or harness.

layers.title: Bronze
layers.purpose: Keep every record exactly as delivered, traceable to its delivery, so anything later can be rebuilt.

challenges.title: Changing data on the way in
challenges.goes_wrong: Cleaning or removing duplicates in bronze destroys the evidence needed to rebuild or audit.
challenges.example: Stream replays and late readings are kept and flagged, not dropped.
challenges.solution: Bronze is append-only and raw; cleaning starts in silver.

challenges.title: Rows that cannot be traced
challenges.goes_wrong: Nobody can say which file or run a row came from.
challenges.example: Every bronze row carries its batch key, run id, source file and window.
challenges.solution: Load metadata on every row, and every run recorded with its configuration.

challenges.title: Personal data stored in clear text
challenges.goes_wrong: The rawest layer becomes the biggest privacy risk.
challenges.example: Dealer contact columns.
challenges.solution: Restricted columns are tokenised before the first write; the token key lives outside code.

challenges.title: Replays and late events
challenges.goes_wrong: Dropping them hides problems; keeping them unflagged doubles counts downstream.
challenges.example: Day 3, 188 readings up to 90 seconds late; day 13, a 45-minute stream replay.
challenges.solution: Kept as delivered with arrival time and position; silver applies event time and de-duplication.

challenges.title: Table layout decay
challenges.goes_wrong: Thousands of small files make every read slow.
challenges.example: Many small lab files a day.
challenges.solution: Automatic clustering and maintenance declared once in the binding, not hand-written jobs.

adr.title: Table layout: automatic clustering and automatic maintenance

anti_patterns.title: Cleaning or removing duplicates in bronze
anti_patterns.why: A cleaned bronze no longer shows what the source sent, so a cleaning bug can never be undone by replay.
anti_patterns.instead: Keep bronze raw and do every cleaning step in the bronze-to-silver engine.

anti_patterns.title: Personal data in clear text in bronze
anti_patterns.why: Bronze is kept for a long time as the source for replays, so anything personal stored there in clear text stays exposed.
anti_patterns.instead: Tokenise in the lander and keep the clear value only in the token vault.

anti_patterns.title: Partitioning and hand-written OPTIMIZE jobs
anti_patterns.why: Partitions picked by hand often create many small files, and maintenance jobs are extra code to run.
anti_patterns.instead: Use automatic clustering and leave upkeep to the platform's automatic optimization.

layers.title: Bronze to silver
layers.purpose: Make one source faithful (typed, de-duplicated, history kept, deletes marked) with the same steps for every source.

challenges.title: A different pipeline per table
challenges.goes_wrong: Every table gets its own hand-written code, so each fixes the same problems differently.
challenges.example: Nine tyre datasets, one engine.
challenges.solution: One engine with thirteen standard stages driven by settings; stages are pure functions and reads and writes happen only at the edges.

adr.title: Thirteen standard stages from bronze to silver
IO only at the edges; stages are pure functions

challenges.title: Changes arriving out of order
challenges.goes_wrong: An older change applied after a newer one overwrites the current value.
challenges.example: Day 8, a promised-date change from earlier arrives after a newer one.
challenges.solution: History is ordered by the source's own sequence, never by arrival; the late change is inserted in its place.

challenges.title: Deletes
challenges.goes_wrong: Deleted rows are either lost from history or still counted.
challenges.example: Day 4, five order lines deleted.
challenges.solution: Deletes are soft (marked, kept joinable) and flow through to derived tables.

adr.title: History kind follows dataset kind; deletes are soft

challenges.title: Duplicates inside the source and replayed events
challenges.goes_wrong: The same reading or row counted twice.
challenges.example: Day 13, 19,440 replayed readings.
challenges.solution: De-duplicate by the declared key (for example the reading id) with a declared rule for which copy wins.

challenges.title: A bad full copy
challenges.goes_wrong: A short copy marks hundreds of records deleted.
challenges.example: Day 9, 720 of 1,800 materials missing.
challenges.solution: The mass-delete guard compares the copy with silver's current keys and holds the batch above the declared share.

challenges.title: Bad values
challenges.goes_wrong: Values that fail a rule are silently nulled or dropped, or one bad row stops the whole load.
challenges.example: An impossible cure temperature in a press reading.
challenges.solution: Rules in configuration with a severity that sets the action (warn, quarantine, block); quarantined rows are reviewed and released through the same checks.

adr.title: Quality severity sets the action

challenges.title: A bad load that got through
challenges.goes_wrong: Found days later, after good loads built on it; restoring old versions throws the good loads away.
challenges.example: The day-9 short copy slipping past the guard.
challenges.solution: Void the batch, rebuild the silver table from bronze, rerun the gold windows that use it; recon and known answers prove it.

adr.title: Recover a bad load by voiding it and rerunning from bronze

challenges.title: Columns lost on the way
challenges.goes_wrong: A hand-picked column list silently drops a column a consumer needs.
challenges.example: A new contract column never reaches silver.
challenges.solution: Every contract column reaches silver unless a selection is declared.

adr.title: Silver takes all columns by default

anti_patterns.title: Free-form SQL in bronze to silver
anti_patterns.why: Hand-written SQL per table brings back the copy-paste pipelines the engine replaced, and it cannot be unit-tested.
anti_patterns.instead: Declare the need as a setting; if no setting fits, add a tested stage option to the engine for everyone.

anti_patterns.title: Silently dropping or nulling bad values
anti_patterns.why: Rows that vanish quietly make gold totals wrong with no trace of why.
anti_patterns.instead: Quarantine the row with its reason and let a steward release it once fixed.

anti_patterns.title: Joining sources or adding business logic in silver
anti_patterns.why: Silver is source-aligned; mixing sources there blurs ownership and breaks replays per source.
anti_patterns.instead: Combine sources in gold, inside a fact's pure build() function.

anti_patterns.title: A copy-pasted pipeline per table
anti_patterns.why: A fix must be made fifty times, and the copies drift apart.
anti_patterns.instead: Add the table as metadata to the common pipeline or harness.

layers.title: Silver
layers.purpose: Hold each source's truth, cleaned and with history, without mixing sources yet.

challenges.title: Conforming too early
challenges.goes_wrong: Joining sources in silver ties them together, so one late source blocks another and changes ripple everywhere.
challenges.example: Orders and dealers stay separate in silver.
challenges.solution: Silver is source-aligned; conforming and joining happen in gold. Data flows one way through the layers.

adr.title: Silver is source-aligned; conforming happens in gold

challenges.title: The wrong kind of history
challenges.goes_wrong: History kept where it is not needed, or lost where it is.
challenges.example: Dealer region keeps history; a phone number is simply overwritten.
challenges.solution: History kind per dataset (and per attribute where needed) is declared; the engine applies it.

adr.title: History kind follows dataset kind; deletes are soft

challenges.title: Late stream events
challenges.goes_wrong: Late readings land in the wrong hour or are dropped.
challenges.example: Day 3, 188 late readings.
challenges.solution: Event time with a declared late allowance; readings counted in their event hour.

challenges.title: Drift nobody sees
challenges.goes_wrong: A column's values shift slowly and nothing notices until a report is wrong.
challenges.example: Scrap reason codes changing mix.
challenges.solution: Every dataset is profiled on load and drift is visible and alertable.

challenges.title: Writes that are not repeatable
challenges.goes_wrong: A rerun adds rows or versions.
challenges.example: Rerunning day 8.
challenges.solution: Merge on a row key computed from the data; the bookmark records which bronze batches each run consumed.

anti_patterns.title: Joining sources or adding business logic in silver
anti_patterns.why: Silver is source-aligned; mixing sources there blurs ownership and breaks replays per source.
anti_patterns.instead: Combine sources in gold, inside a fact's pure build() function.

anti_patterns.title: Chaining layers by clock time
anti_patterns.why: Starting silver at 03:00 because bronze usually ends by 02:30 breaks the first night bronze runs late, and nobody notices.
anti_patterns.instead: Trigger on data readiness: the batch-ready marker for silver, input bookmarks for gold.

anti_patterns.title: Partitioning and hand-written OPTIMIZE jobs
anti_patterns.why: Partitions picked by hand often create many small files, and maintenance jobs are extra code to run.
anti_patterns.instead: Use automatic clustering and leave upkeep to the platform's automatic optimization.

layers.title: Silver to gold
layers.purpose: Make several sources agree on keys, grain, time and meaning, without losing or doubling a row.

challenges.title: Rows dropped in joins
challenges.goes_wrong: An inner join to a missing dealer or material silently drops sales.
challenges.example: Sales naming a dealer not yet in the dealer table.
challenges.solution: Left join plus an unknown member; rows in must equal rows out, with unmatched rows and duplicate keys counted separately so they cannot cancel out.

adr.title: Deterministic hash surrogate keys with reserved members -1 and -2

challenges.title: Conforming keys across sources
challenges.goes_wrong: The same customer has different codes in different systems, so totals split or double.
challenges.example: An order-system customer code, a dealer interface id and a name in partner files.
challenges.solution: Mapping tables kept by a steward, with suggested matches; deterministic hash surrogate keys.

adr.title: Deterministic hash surrogate keys with reserved members -1 and -2

challenges.title: Grain and double counting
challenges.goes_wrong: Joining one to many multiplies quantities.
challenges.example: Order lines joined to deliveries.
challenges.solution: Grain declared per fact and tested unique; joins aggregated to the fact's grain first; fan-out detected from captured query plans.

challenges.title: Which version of history applies
challenges.goes_wrong: A sale is joined to today's dealer region instead of the region on the day of the sale.
challenges.example: A dealer moving region mid-month.
challenges.solution: Joins as of the event date on history tables.

adr.title: History dimensions are joined as of the event

challenges.title: Completeness across sources
challenges.goes_wrong: Four of six inputs have arrived; publishing gives partial numbers that look final.
challenges.example: Lab results four hours late; partner files a day late.
challenges.solution: Inputs declared per fact, a completeness signal per input, and a declared policy per fact (wait, publish provisional, or wait then provisional with a maximum wait); every window carries a complete flag.

adr.title: A gold window is complete only when every input has caught up

challenges.title: Late facts and restatements
challenges.goes_wrong: October's numbers change in November, or late rows are ignored.
challenges.example: Day 5, dealer D-0042's October file.
challenges.solution: Recompute exactly the windows the new data touched (replace, never append) and log the restatement.

adr.title: Facts are tables built by window recompute; materialised views only for simple aggregates

challenges.title: Late reference data
challenges.goes_wrong: A fact arrives before its dealer exists and is dropped or keyed wrong.
challenges.example: Days 11 and 12, new dealer D-9001.
challenges.solution: Unknown member first, re-keyed when the dealer arrives.

challenges.title: Corrections
challenges.goes_wrong: The source fixes a past value and old reports silently change, or never change.
challenges.example: Day 10, twelve promised dates corrected.
challenges.solution: Corrections live in their own table and reach gold only for the windows their plan names, logged as a restatement.

adr.title: Corrections live in their own table and reach gold through a backfill plan

challenges.title: Deletes reaching gold
challenges.goes_wrong: A deleted line still counts.
challenges.example: The day-4 deleted order lines.
challenges.solution: Gold reads current, non-deleted rows when windows recompute.

challenges.title: Time zones and business calendars
challenges.goes_wrong: Days cut at the wrong hour; fiscal periods computed differently in each report.
challenges.example: Plants in India and Hungary.
challenges.solution: Business date per plant and one shared calendar, declared once.

challenges.title: Recompute cost
challenges.goes_wrong: Rebuilding everything every night is slow and costly.
challenges.example: Fourteen days of order lines.
challenges.solution: Only the windows the new data touched are recomputed.

challenges.title: Functional join mistakes in hand-written queries
challenges.goes_wrong: Inner instead of left, a wrong key, a many-to-many join; the query runs and the numbers are wrong.
challenges.example: Two dealers missing and one duplicated, so the net row count looks almost normal.
challenges.solution: Declared join shapes checked against captured plans and observed counts of unmatched rows and duplicate keys.

challenges.title: Proving gold is right
challenges.goes_wrong: A quiet two percent error goes unnoticed for months.
challenges.example: OTIF south November must equal 0.8961.
challenges.solution: Known answers from the synthetic world in tests; reconciliation from silver to gold in production.

anti_patterns.title: Inner join from fact to dimension
anti_patterns.why: Rows whose dimension has not arrived simply vanish, and totals quietly drop.
anti_patterns.instead: Left join, give missing matches surrogate key -1, measure the orphan rate and re-key on the next recompute.

anti_patterns.title: Joining incremental to incremental
anti_patterns.why: Joining only the new rows of one input to only the new rows of another misses every match that arrived in a different batch.
anti_patterns.instead: Detect changed windows incrementally, then read every input in full for those windows.

anti_patterns.title: Appending to gold facts
anti_patterns.why: Every retry or late file double-counts.
anti_patterns.instead: Replace the whole window, or MERGE on the grain key.

anti_patterns.title: Joining an SCD2 dimension to its current row only
anti_patterns.why: Last year's sales get this year's customer region, so history is rewritten.
anti_patterns.instead: Join where event time is between valid_from and valid_to.

anti_patterns.title: One giant SQL notebook mixing IO and logic
anti_patterns.why: It cannot be unit-tested, reused or reviewed in parts.
anti_patterns.instead: Write a pure build(inputs) function and let the harness do reads and writes.

anti_patterns.title: Publishing before inputs are complete
anti_patterns.why: Users see half a day and make decisions on it.
anti_patterns.instead: Publish a window only when every input bookmark has passed its end.

anti_patterns.title: Fixing data by hand in gold
anti_patterns.why: The fix is overwritten on the next rebuild and leaves no audit trail.
anti_patterns.instead: Add a row to the corrections table and run the backfill plan.

layers.title: Gold
layers.purpose: Model the business correctly (grain, fact type, shared dimensions, history) and publish only what passed its checks.

challenges.title: Undeclared grain
challenges.goes_wrong: Nobody can say what one row means, so numbers cannot be added up safely.
challenges.example: Is OTIF per order line or per delivery?
challenges.solution: Grain declared per fact and tested unique; a grain is suggested from key profiling and confirmed by the modeller.

challenges.title: The wrong fact type
challenges.goes_wrong: Snapshots summed over time, or an order's current stage impossible to answer.
challenges.example: Sales are transactions; inventory is a periodic snapshot; order to delivery is an accumulating snapshot.
challenges.solution: Fact type declared per fact; the harness builds the matching pattern.

challenges.title: Dimensions that do not conform
challenges.goes_wrong: Two dashboards disagree on the same region.
challenges.example: One plant dimension shared by OTIF and scrap.
challenges.solution: Shared dimensions declared once; the bus matrix (which facts share which dimensions) generated from the declarations.

challenges.title: History per attribute
challenges.goes_wrong: Sales move to a new region retroactively, or history that matters is lost.
challenges.example: Dealer region keeps history; phone does not.
challenges.solution: History type declared per attribute; joins as of the event.

challenges.title: Roles, bridges and facts about absence
challenges.goes_wrong: Order date and delivery date confused; a dealer in two groups counted twice; nothing counts what did not happen.
challenges.example: One date dimension used as order, promised and delivery date.
challenges.solution: Role-playing dimensions, bridge tables with weights and factless facts declared and generated; which absences matter is a business decision.

challenges.title: Keys that change on every rebuild
challenges.goes_wrong: Identity or sequence keys differ after a rerun, breaking every join and saved report.
challenges.example: Rebuilding gold after a correction.
challenges.solution: Deterministic hash surrogate keys with reserved members for unknown and not applicable.

adr.title: Deterministic hash surrogate keys with reserved members -1 and -2

challenges.title: Publishing unchecked numbers
challenges.goes_wrong: A broken build reaches dashboards before anyone looks.
challenges.example: A gold window with orphan rows above the limit.
challenges.solution: Checks before publish (keys, totals against the build, orphan rate); a failure publishes nothing.

anti_patterns.title: Undeclared grain
anti_patterns.why: Nobody can tell a duplicate from a valid row, and measures get summed twice.
anti_patterns.instead: Declare the grain in metadata and check uniqueness before publish.

anti_patterns.title: One wide table as the only gold
anti_patterns.why: A single wide table repeats dimension values, is hard to change, and hides grain.
anti_patterns.instead: Build a star schema; add a wide view or a semantic-layer view on top when a use case needs it.

anti_patterns.title: Identity or sequence surrogate keys
anti_patterns.why: Keys change on every rebuild and differ between environments, breaking joins and comparisons.
anti_patterns.instead: Hash of source + business key (+ valid_from for SCD type 2).

anti_patterns.title: Quality checks only in silver
anti_patterns.why: Joins and aggregates create their own errors (orphans, double counts) that silver checks can never see.
anti_patterns.instead: Check grain, orphan rate, reconciliation and completeness in gold too.

anti_patterns.title: Materialized views for everything
anti_patterns.why: Multi-input materialized views give no control over windows, completeness or quality, and can cost more to refresh.
anti_patterns.instead: Use a table written by the window recompute job.

anti_patterns.title: Dropping business keys from facts
anti_patterns.why: Without them, re-keying orphans and tracing a row back to the source are impossible.
anti_patterns.instead: Keep both the business key and the surrogate key.

layers.title: Gold to semantic
layers.purpose: Turn gold into numbers people use, each defined once, aggregated correctly and honest about completeness.

challenges.title: Aggregating ratios wrongly
challenges.goes_wrong: Averaging OTIF percentages across plants gives the wrong total; inventory summed over months is meaningless.
challenges.example: OTIF by region.
challenges.solution: Each measure declares whether it is additive, semi-additive or non-additive; ratios are built from their parts.

challenges.title: One number, many definitions
challenges.goes_wrong: The dashboard, the conversation interface and a spreadsheet each compute OTIF differently.
challenges.example: OTIF counting or not counting cancelled lines.
challenges.solution: One certified definition per metric, generated from the manifest, as the only source for every consumer.

adr.title: Metrics are certified before conversation interfaces and agents use them

challenges.title: Comparing across facts
challenges.goes_wrong: OTIF and sales by region cannot be compared because the regions differ.
challenges.example: Region from the dealer table versus region from the plant table.
challenges.solution: Conformed dimensions declared once and reused by every metric.

challenges.title: Time intelligence
challenges.goes_wrong: Year to date and fiscal periods computed differently each time.
challenges.example: Fiscal year starting in April.
challenges.solution: One shared calendar with business dates and fiscal periods.

challenges.title: Incomplete windows inside a ratio
challenges.goes_wrong: Lines not yet due count as missed, so the ratio looks worse than the truth.
challenges.example: OTIF counted every line of the month; over complete windows it is 0.8961.
challenges.solution: Ratios count complete windows only; counts of rows still cover every row.

anti_patterns.title: Business logic in BI tools or views
anti_patterns.why: The same metric gets computed differently in each dashboard, and nobody can test it.
anti_patterns.instead: Put calculations in gold build() or in the semantic layer's metric definitions.

anti_patterns.title: One wide table as the only gold
anti_patterns.why: A single wide table repeats dimension values, is hard to change, and hides grain.
anti_patterns.instead: Build a star schema; add a wide view or a semantic-layer view on top when a use case needs it.

layers.title: Semantic layer
layers.purpose: Keep every business definition in one governed place that people, tools and agents all read.

challenges.title: Definitions nobody agreed
challenges.goes_wrong: Two teams certify different OTIF formulas.
challenges.example: Partial deliveries counted or not.
challenges.solution: The tool versions, certifies and tests definitions and flags two that disagree; the definition itself is a business decision.

adr.title: Metrics are certified before conversation interfaces and agents use them

challenges.title: Definitions that change silently
challenges.goes_wrong: Last year's number changes and nobody knows why.
challenges.example: OTIF definition changed in January.
challenges.solution: Versioned definitions with a restatement note.

challenges.title: Words people actually use
challenges.goes_wrong: Questions in plain language miss because people say sell-through, sell-out or sales.
challenges.example: Synonyms for OTIF.
challenges.solution: Synonyms and descriptions declared with each metric; new synonyms suggested from questions asked.

challenges.title: Security inside metrics
challenges.goes_wrong: A regional manager sees other regions' totals through an aggregate.
challenges.example: Region-level sales.
challenges.solution: Row filters declared once and applied in every metric.

challenges.title: Provisional numbers that look final
challenges.goes_wrong: A partial window is read as final.
challenges.example: Sales while one dealer's file is missing.
challenges.solution: The complete flag from gold is carried into every metric and shown.

anti_patterns.title: Business logic in BI tools or views
anti_patterns.why: The same metric gets computed differently in each dashboard, and nobody can test it.
anti_patterns.instead: Put calculations in gold build() or in the semantic layer's metric definitions.

anti_patterns.title: Pointing a conversational query tool at raw silver tables
anti_patterns.why: The tool then guesses joins and meanings and gives plausible but wrong answers.
anti_patterns.instead: Point it at metric definitions and described gold tables.

layers.title: Semantic to experiences
layers.purpose: Serve dashboards, conversation interfaces, agents and apps the same certified numbers, cheaply and visibly fresh.

challenges.title: Dashboards re-querying raw tables
challenges.goes_wrong: Every open and every click scans large raw tables, and the warehouse bill grows with viewers.
challenges.example: A monitoring dashboard over raw platform telemetry.
challenges.solution: Dashboards read certified definitions over compact summary tables, with stored results refreshed when data changes.

challenges.title: A conversation interface roaming raw tables
challenges.goes_wrong: Plain-language questions produce heavy or wrong queries on raw data.
challenges.example: Asking for OTIF straight from silver.
challenges.solution: The conversation interface sees only certified definitions and verified functions for frequent questions.

challenges.title: One number, many tools
challenges.goes_wrong: The dashboard, the conversation interface and an agent disagree.
challenges.example: OTIF south November.
challenges.solution: All of them read the same certified definitions; known answers are tested.

challenges.title: Agents writing their own queries
challenges.goes_wrong: An agent's ad-hoc query is untested, unpermissioned and can be wrong.
challenges.example: A triage agent explaining a failed run.
challenges.solution: Agents call typed tools with fixed, tested queries; anything they propose goes to the owner's gate.

adr.title: Agents propose, gates decide; agents follow the same kernel and adapter split

challenges.title: The cost of looking
challenges.goes_wrong: Watching and asking cost more than the pipelines themselves.
challenges.example: A monitoring template and plain-language questions over raw telemetry.
challenges.solution: Summary tables, stored results and verified functions under monitoring and conversation screens.

challenges.title: Stale screens
challenges.goes_wrong: A cached screen shows yesterday's number as today's.
challenges.example: A dashboard cached before a restatement.
challenges.solution: Refresh on data change; freshness and the provisional flag shown on the screen.

challenges.title: Rebuilding what the platform gives
challenges.goes_wrong: A custom portal duplicates dashboards and catalog screens and falls behind.
challenges.example: Viewing dashboards in a custom app.
challenges.solution: Native screens for viewing; our own app only for actions (alerts, approvals, quarantine release, recovery, declarations).

anti_patterns.title: Business logic in BI tools or views
anti_patterns.why: The same metric gets computed differently in each dashboard, and nobody can test it.
anti_patterns.instead: Put calculations in gold build() or in the semantic layer's metric definitions.

anti_patterns.title: Pointing a conversational query tool at raw silver tables
anti_patterns.why: The tool then guesses joins and meanings and gives plausible but wrong answers.
anti_patterns.instead: Point it at metric definitions and described gold tables.

anti_patterns.title: Agents querying tables directly
anti_patterns.why: Untested, unpermissioned queries; answers that differ from the dashboard.
anti_patterns.instead: Typed tools over certified definitions, with proposals going to a gate.

anti_patterns.title: A custom portal that rebuilds native dashboards
anti_patterns.why: Twice the work, and it drifts from the governed screens.
anti_patterns.instead: Link out to native screens; build only screens that take actions.
